newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran-Kazakh oil swap deal starts with trial cargoes.
newsitem.headline: Iran-Kazakh oil swap deal starts with trial cargoes.

text.p: Kazakhstan has started shipping trial cargoes of oil across the Caspian Sea to Iran as part of a proposed oil exchange deal between the two states, an Iranian energy official said on Monday.

"The contract started on January 1, but to have everything in order we need to have some trial cargoes," Hojjatollah Ghanimifard, director of international affairs at the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), told Reuters in an interview.
The United States, which has imposed sanctions against Iran after accusing it of supporting terrorism, is concerned about the deal as some U.S. oil firms are investing in Kazakh oil projects.

The trial shipments from Kazakhstan so far have amounted to less than 15,000 tonnes of "Kazakh Blend" crude, below the 120,000 to 150,000 tonnes required to make up the first full tanker of Iranian crude that would be made available to Kazakhstan by NIOC under the deal.
"The regularity of the (Kazakh) shipping is the most important factor in the whole contract because there should not be any disruption (to Iranian refineries)," Ghanimifard said.
"This needs some practice. I think this is a warm-up phase for this swap contract," he added. "They have to ship every day one cargo by the amount they have accepted," he added.

The swap deal envisages Kazakhstan supplying an initial two million tonnes a year of crude oil to Iran's Tehran and Tabriz refineries in exchange for access to a similar quantity of Iranian Light crude primarily at export facilities in the Gulf.

Iran President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev signed the deal in May but the start of the contract has been held up by negotiations over operational and commercial details.

By being able to lift Iranian crude from the Gulf to international hard-currency export markets, Kazakhstan will be able to reduce its dependence on Russia as the land route for Almaty's growing production of crude.
